_comment: Scenario presets to GENERATE from the vanilla 1836 start (tools/extract_presets.ps1 -> ui/presets.js). Each entry is one country's WHOLE MARKET: the lead country plus every subject that shares its market (all subject types share the overlord's market unless a `grant_own_market` pact exists — read live from common/history/diplomacy/00_subject_relationships.txt). 'market_add' / 'market_drop' are manual overrides on that member list (tags, no c: prefix). 'sol' is the per-class wealth level whose buy package the class consumes (defaults below); pop demand is then scaled in the UI by the session 'vanilla-fit' knob. The UI always offers a built-in 'Empty' preset on top of these.

defaults._year_comment: Scenario year. Which goods pops may want defaults from this ALONE (a good is available once some building x PM that makes it can exist anywhere — a market imports what it cannot produce, so this is deliberately NOT the lead country's research). Per preset: 'year', plus 'unlock_add' / 'unlock_drop' arrays to force individual goods on/off for anything the calendar can't know (e.g. "unlock_drop": ["clippers"] for a landlocked market).
defaults._class_mult_comment: Optional overrides for how much of its buy package a class brings to the market. Omitted classes use the game's own numbers where they exist: peasants = consumption_mult from common/pop_types/peasants.txt (0.05). 'slaves' is our modelling choice — the game has no consumption_mult for them.

presets._comment: PLACEHOLDER scenarios - synthetic, NOT derived from any country. One level of every ordinary building so that every production chain is present exactly once, which is what BE-solving wants. Deliberately uniform and deliberately crude: diversify them later. A `placeholder` block replaces `country`/`measured_market` entirely. lower_sol drives everything: middle = 1.5x, upper = 3x (per the user's rule), and the base wage comes from FINDINGS F26, base = exp((SoL-37.43)/10.49). `unlock` is one of basic | steamers | electricity | all.
presets.label: Placeholder SoL 10

placeholder_defaults._comment: Shared by every `placeholder` preset. Pops are flat counts; within-stratum variation is the UI's own SOL_SPREAD, not something the preset carries. peasant_sol_offset is added to lower_sol - measured 1836 puts peasants within ~0.5 of the lower stratum either way (Belgium +0.5, Austria -0.4), so 0 is the honest default rather than a guess.
placeholder_defaults._exclude_comment: Company headquarters are excluded as SPECIAL: they exist only once a company is formed, so they are not part of any ordinary chain. Manor houses and financial districts are kept - they are ordinary ownership buildings, they employ the upper stratum this scenario has, and they carry no market goods either way.
